name: Plucking, threading and waxing eyebrows

card.summary: The three main ways of removing stray eyebrow hair to shape the brow line and frame the eyes more cleanly.
card.note: Threading and waxing can cause skin irritation or infection; case reports include warts and molluscum.

quick.overview:
Plucking, threading and waxing are epilation methods that remove eyebrow hair from the follicle. They are the standard ways of tidying and shaping brows, clearing stray hairs and defining the arch and tail.

Tweezing removes single hairs, threading uses a twisted cotton thread to lift short rows of hair, and waxing removes a strip of hair at once. Regrowth takes weeks, so shape lasts until the next session. Dermatology literature classes all three as temporary methods.
quick.how: Plucking is done at home with tweezers, hair by hair. Threading is typically done by a trained technician with a doubled, twisted thread rolled along the skin, and is often chosen for crisp lines. Waxing, done at a salon or at home, removes many hairs at once. People often combine a brow pencil or gel with any of these to complete the look; sessions repeat every few weeks.
quick.risks: The main drawback reported is pain, as several hairs are removed at once. Skin irritation, redness and ingrown hairs occur, and dermatology case reports describe flat warts and molluscum contagiosum appearing along the brow line after threading, with spread of infection a proposed mechanism. Hairs removed by repeated plucking may regrow thinner for some people, a concern raised in forums. Clean tools and a trained provider are the usual hygiene recommendations.

lead: Plucking, threading and waxing are the three common ways of removing eyebrow hair at the root, and they are the usual routes to a defined brow shape. Dermatology reviews classify plucking, threading, waxing and sugaring as epilation techniques, which remove the hair shaft and bulb and are temporary [1].

Plucking uses tweezers to remove single hairs. Threading, which originated in India and the Middle East, rolls a twisted thread over the skin to remove short rows of hair, and became popular in the West from the late 1980s [2]. Waxing lifts hair with a strip. Shaped brows are used to frame the eyes, balance the face and clean up the brow line.

Reports in dermatology journals describe complications of threading, including warts and molluscum lesions along the eyebrow after sessions [3][4]. On looksmax.org, users discuss whether regular plucking is part of a grooming routine or a "looksmin"; some men report that tidying the unibrow and stray hairs improves their look [5].

chain: Stray hair is removed from the follicle
Brow edges and arch are cleaned up
Defined, symmetrical-looking brows that frame the eyes
angle.text: Removing hair outside the intended brow line gives a cleaner outline, and the effect lasts until regrowth, usually several weeks. Threading, tweezing and waxing differ in precision, speed and pain.

infobox: India and Middle East; West from 1980s

paras: Tweezers remove individual hairs, which allows fine control of shape and is the most common home method [1].

A thin cotton or polyester thread is doubled and twisted, then rolled over hair to pull it from the follicle. It can remove short rows of hair, is regarded as precise, and is described as gentler on the skin than waxing; it is less suited to arms and legs where hair is coarse and plentiful [2]. In some cultures it marks rites of passage such as preparing for marriage, and in Taiwan women traditionally have their faces threaded before Lunar New Year [2].
Warm or cold wax is applied and removed with hair attached. It removes many hairs at once, and reviews list typical adverse events including irritation and burns [1].

Threading reached Germany in the 1980s through Iranian beautician Parastu Amiri and spread across Europe; in the US it grew from the late 1980s as immigrant-owned studios opened in large cities [2]. The Guardian reported that UK online searches for threading services rose 50 percent in 2015 [2].

No controlled trials compare brow-shaping methods head to head. A literature review of hair removal practices describes each method's advantages and adverse events and notes that most efficacy studies involve darker hair and fairer skin [1]. Case-based literature on threading includes a review of its seldom-discussed complications [3], a report of flat warts (verruca plana) after threading [6], and a series of eight patients, three men and five women, who developed molluscum lesions along the brow after threading [4].

Pain is the main drawback, because several hairs are removed at once [2]. Dermatology reports link threading to localised skin infections spreading along the brow line [3][4][6]. Hair removal reviews list irritation, folliculitis and pigment changes among the adverse events for epilation methods [1].

Users of looksmax.org discuss brow plucking as part of grooming and whether it counts as a "looksmin" [5]. Brow shape is widely treated in the community as an inexpensive way to adjust the look of the eye area.

lore.intro: Brow grooming is discussed on looksmax.org as a basic part of grooming, with debate over whether plucking is worthwhile.[5]

claims.claim: Plucking stray brow hairs is a cheap way to look better
claims.believers: Forum users say tidying the brow line and unibrow sharpens the face and is a low-cost step.[5]
claims.experts: No controlled studies assess the effect of brow shaping on attractiveness; reviews cover technique and adverse events only.[1]
